# search-research

A research page on the 2026 frontier of corpus search and tagging — for a
~30k-doc personal corpus of transcripts, internal memos, and Slack
messages. Local-first bias, opinionated, all sources cited.

## what to read first

- `index.html` — the full research page, served at http://127.0.0.1:8424
- `agents.json` — production-agent stack table (Goose, Claude Code, Hermes,
  Honcho, Letta, Mem0, Zep, Cognee, LangGraph, Dust)
- `papers.json` — frontier paper bibliography by area (embedding, RAG, tagging)
- `stacks.json` — corpus-size keyed stack recommendations (1k / 30k / 1M / 100M)

All four are agent-fetchable. The HTML is enriched with JSON-LD describing
which dataset URLs are which, so an agent that respects `application/ld+json`
can discover the right file without parsing markup.

## the recommended stack (~30k docs, local-first)

```
corpus/                  ← markdown/txt files, source of truth
  *.md (yaml frontmatter for tags)
index.lance/             ← LanceDB single-file store (regeneratable)
config.yaml              ← embedding model + chunking choices
search.py                ← ~150 lines, exposes index() / search() / tag()
```

Four dependencies: `lancedb`, `ollama`, `pyyaml`, `click`.
Default embedding: `nomic-embed-text:v1.5` via Ollama.
Default reranker: none in v1; add `bge-reranker-v2-gemma` if measured-needed.
Tagging: BERTopic for clustering, prototype networks for k-NN, Cleanlab
for label hygiene. LLM (Haiku) only as fallback for ambiguous cases.

## key insight

The corpus folder is the source of truth. The vector index is
**regeneratable** at any time from the corpus. That single property is
what keeps the whole stack pluggable: you can swap the embedding model,
swap the vector store, swap the search frontend, all by re-running
`reindex` against the same files.

## what to skip

- 2023-style RAG pipeline (chunk → embed → store → retrieve → rerank → stuff → synthesize) — replaced by hybrid retrieval + agentic search-as-tool
- Pure long-context "stuff everything in" — RULER and Lost-in-the-Middle show 30-50% accuracy drop past 200k tokens
- Heavy frameworks (LlamaIndex, Haystack) at this scale — complexity cost > time saved
- Managed vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate) at this scale — pay-rent SaaS for capacity unused
- Multi-vector / late-interaction (ColBERT v2) — mostly displaced by single-vector + hybrid + reranker
- LLM-tagging every doc upfront — use embedding-classifier, LLM-fallback only on ambiguous (~$30 vs $300+)

## what production agents actually use

See `agents.json` for the full table. Patterns:
- No consensus on storage backend — choose by deployment shape
- Almost no one ships their own embeddings — all defer to OpenAI/Ollama
- Memory tier splits (short-term vs long-term) are real and worth copying
- Filesystem-based memory (Anthropic, Claude Code) is having a moment for
  auditability and portability — validates the "corpus as source of truth"
  approach

## frontier papers (must-read)

- arXiv:2409.04701 — Late Chunking
- arXiv:2412.15605 — Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG)
- arXiv:2501.09136 — Agentic RAG survey
- arXiv:2307.03172 — Lost in the Middle
- arXiv:2404.06654 — RULER long-context benchmark

Full annotated list in `papers.json`.
